1.why: Reset tokens are stored with an accountId and password change applies only to that account via a sid-bound grant after consume.

2.why: A reset code maps to one ResetRecord/accountId and is deleted on use, so it does not authorize reset for arbitrary other users.

3.why: Password reset updates the hash and current session fields only; no code invalidates other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords use Argon2id, but reset codes and session/user records are plain in-memory Map values without encryption.

6.why: Simulated delivery log only includes the recovery code message and does not add extra account profile fields.

7.why: Inputs are normalized/length-limited via normalizeEmail, text, rawString checks, and client display uses textContent.

8.why: Recovery links are built only as same-origin /?token=... from location.origin with encodeURIComponent.

9.why: Simulated email/log content is server-fixed text plus random code, not user-supplied HTML/scripts.

10.why: API responses and the demo Logs panel intentionally expose deliveryCode, logMessage, and MFA codes.

11.why: Argon2id hashes are used at runtime, but the fixture password hash and fixed MFA value 246810 are embedded in source/logic.

12.why: Login is refused unless this session completed a verified reset for the demo account; no default password login path is enabled.

13.why: rateLimit is applied to reset requests, verification, login, and MFA with lockouts after repeated attempts.

14.why: request-reset always returns the same generic success style message whether or not the email matches an account.

15.why: Codes are randomHex(32), single-use with expiry, and stored with the target accountId when an account exists.
